turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Price section didn't work. Too many numbers at too many sizes. Couldn't spot the total without reading every label."

We want to understand what you meant by "couldn't spot the total without reading every label", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The Total row sits at the bottom of the summary section with no visual separation or distinct zone to set it apart from the Subtotal and Shipping rows above it.

B) The Total label appears in bold but its corresponding figure ($288.99) is displayed at the same size as the Subtotal figure directly above it, giving both numbers equal visual weight in the layout.

C) The Order Summary section has no clear structural break — item prices, Subtotal, and Total are all stacked within a single undivided block, so the Total has no dedicated area that signals it as the final number.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to).

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.

Looking at that right-hand column specifically, the $288.99 figure appears twice — once next to Subtotal and once next to Total — at what looks like the same size. Which of those two instances did your eye land on first?
turns.a: Subtotal, tax, total — all different sizes. No obvious main number. Couldn't tell which was the total at a glance.

turns.q: If someone arrived at this layout needing to confirm the amount they're about to be charged before filling in their card details, what would that scanning process look like given that the Subtotal and Total figures are the same size?
turns.a: Nearly moved on without confirming the total. Too many sizes at similar weights — couldn't tell which was the main one. Stopped and read each label to confirm.

turns.q: If the label-reading problem you described was completely solved — "Total" bold, its $288.99 visually distinct from the Subtotal figure — would that be enough, or is there something about how that whole bottom row sits within the same undivided block as Subtotal and Shipping that would still bother you?
turns.a: Total needs to be the largest number in the section — obviously so. Line items all the same size, clearly smaller. Secondary text smaller still. That's a typographic scale. Right now there are five sizes in that section. There should be three.
